Against Elfsborg, Mjällby primarily built up from a 3-2-4-1 / 3-2-2-3 / 3-trapezoid-3 structure. As Elfsborg repeatedly transitioned from a 4-2-3-1 midfield block into active pressing, supportive movements from the holding midfielders were required. Gustafson and Leandersson, the two sixes in this match, repeatedly dropped into the build-up zone, at times positioning themselves in front of the first pressing line. This made Mjällby more resistant to pressure and simultaneously stretched the centre. As a consequence, Mjällby were able to play through the resulting 4-2-4 press via the centre, finding striker Bergström or one of the number tens, often through lay-offs.

Mjällby build up in a 3-2-4-1 against Elfsborg’s 4-2-4 mid-block. By having the number sixes drop towards the ball, a local overload is created and the space between the lines is stretched.

Against Elfsborg, Mjällby did not stretch the centre only through deeper positioning of the holding midfielders. Wider positioning of both the sixes and the number tens was also used to open direct passing lanes to striker Bergström through the now-expanded central areas. Mjällby are repeatedly able to play through the centre precisely because of these shifts from narrower to wider positions, which stretch the opponent again. Once the opponent is stretched, the diagonal pass through the centre typically becomes available. If one of the forwards or number tens is found, play can again be progressed through effective lay-off combinations, supported by the strong central occupation.

When the opponent plays with only two holding midfielders, a common solution is to have the eights or central midfielders drop wider, while the fullbacks move inside on the last line. This places the two sixes in a dilemma between protecting the centre and applying pressure. This approach also worked very effectively against Malmö. The two eights in the diamond, Gustafson and Thorell, repeatedly dropped into wide areas, creating constant dilemmas for Malmö’s defensive structure.

Against Malmö’s defensive pressing in a 5-2-3, Mjällby’s number eights drop out wide to become available for passes. This makes the shuttling movements of Malmö’s two number sixes too extensive.

Mjällby’s potential and development.

Recent findings suggest that despite their attractive central play, Mjällby still have significant potential for development in this very area. Especially in earlier matches of the season, the team struggled to consistently exploit appropriate central structures. This was particularly evident in the first leg against AIK. At that time, Mjällby’s play was strongly oriented toward immediate progression. Against AIK, this led to the centre backs frequently playing high balls over the block, even though suitable central structures were available to play through the 5-4-1 block with its very narrow back four. The result was a number of turnovers, which reduced the team’s otherwise existing dominance.

In later matches of the season, such as against Malmö or Elfsborg, Mjällby were far more successful in establishing longer phases of possession, playing less hastily into depth and thus dominating the opponent through controlled ball circulation. Especially against deep-defending opponents, there is considerable potential in suffocating the opposition through tighter spacing and longer possession phases. This is precisely what the next section will focus on.

One of the reasons why Mjällby stand apart from the classic style of European football lies in how they attack a low block. The way Mjällby play against deep-defending opponents is very likely to become more common in the major European leagues over the coming years. The positional play used by most teams is based on stretching specific spaces in order to exploit them afterwards. This works well by repeatedly forcing the opponent to shift until a free player eventually emerges. Against deep blocks over a full 90 minutes, however, this type of possession play often works only to a limited extent, or not at all.

Sources indicate that deep-defending opponents are positioned so compactly around their own goal that decisive spaces are difficult to open. The team in possession can circulate the ball around the block but struggles to find access to a free player through it. Due to the compactness of the defending team, alternative solutions are required. This is also one of the reasons why many teams have returned to using classic centre forwards who are strong in the air and in finishing, and who can be found in the box through crosses even without playing through the tight block.

In a recent development, mjällby, by contrast, usually do not rely on a classic positional or spatial structure when playing into the final third or against a low block. Instead, they very often look to combine through side (/wide) overloads. Especially in the earlier matches of the season, such overloads in the wide zone were clearly visible. These are created through the ball-near outer centre back, the ball-near fullback, the three more advanced central players and the striker. Frequently, the side overload consists of five to six of these players.

It has been revealed that the rest defence is usually formed by the central centre back, the holding midfielder, most often captain Gustavsson, and the ball-far outer centre back. It is important that Mjällby maintain a plus-one advantage in rest defence. If the opponent has only one counter-attacking player, the ball-far outer centre back also steps forward to join in. It is noticeable that on switches of play both outer centre backs regularly push forward, become involved offensively and can create additional danger, including inside the opponent’s penalty area. Box occupation is typically provided by the ball-far fullback and striker Bergström.

Mjällby’s classic pitch occupation against a low block: five to six players overload the ball side, while the far-side outer centre-back, the central centre-back and the number six form the rest defence, with the striker and the far-side full-back occupying the box.

Recent findings suggest that within the side (/wide) overload, positional roles play only a minor part. Instead, the focus is on combining toward the byline. The dynamism of the outer centre back is particularly helpful here. He is almost always involved in play during side overloads. The advantage lies in the momentum he generates by running forward from deeper positions. This presents an additional challenge for the defence, as another player arrives from behind with speed and must be picked up.

Industry observers note that an anchor player is virtually always present and can be found through a backward pass at any time. This allows Mjällby to exit the overload and, by playing back into it, create a new dynamic and stretch the opponent again. The anchor player’s primary role is not to switch play to the far side. He is part of the overload and helps to resolve the tight pressure situation. A player occupying the width on the touchline is also always present. This stretches the opponent within a very small space. Crucially, the anchor role and the wide role rotate. The width is only initially provided by the fullback, while the anchor role is initially taken up by the outer centre back.

In a recent development, also noteworthy is the positioning of the more central players. They look for positions in front of the last line, forcing it to decide whether to step up and apply pressure or to protect depth. If the last line steps forward, depth is attacked with opposite movements, allowing Mjällby to reach the byline more easily.

Within the overload itself, relational principles come to the fore: pass and move patterns (toco y me voy), wall passes/ one-two combinations (tabela), opposite movements and escadinhas in combination with letting the ball run (corta luz). I have linked two example videos on X that illustrate Mjällbys play within side (/wide) overloads.

According to recent reports, (1) M.H. auf X: „(3/8) Mjällby’s wide overloads against a low-block: Using relational principles, Mjällby combine through wide overloads and break down the low block:“ / X.

Sources indicate that (1) M.H. auf X: „(4/8) Mjällby play through wide overloads. One key advantage of involving the outer center backs is improved penalty area occupation:“ / X.

Recent findings suggest that when the ball is played back to the anchor player or moved further away from the overload, this often provokes the opponent to step out. This is followed by a diagonal run in behind from the outside and a high ball over the last line. Because positional assignments have been loosened by the preceding overload, these runs can be made by different players, but always by the player who had been occupying the wide position on the outside. An example video of this pattern is also linked.

(1) M.H. auf X: „(5/8) The backward pass from the wide overload draws out the opponent’s back line. The wide player then typically makes a diagonal run into depth:“ / X.

A major advantage of playing through overloads lies in the tight distances between players. After losing the ball, the opponent must first spread out in order to secure possession. At the same time, Mjällby immediately have a large number of players close to the ball who can apply counterpressing. Over the course of the season, a clear development could be observed in this area. Increasingly, Mjällby were able to suffocate opponents through successful counterpressing actions. The high points came in the matches against Malmö and Elfsborg, where Mjällby were able to regain possession immediately through effective backward pressing after turnovers.

Nevertheless, there is still considerable potential for development here. Mjällby’s play is strongly oriented toward progression. As a result, after taking the lead, they often struggle to control the opponent through possession. Because they repeatedly look to progress toward goal very quickly, this also leads to more turnovers. Especially after going ahead, a useful means of establishing control could be to overload their own build-up zone, creating longer possession phases and forcing the opponent to step up with more players.

According to recent reports, in order to be less predictable when attacking the final third, Mjällby also rely on central play using similar principles and structures to those described earlier against a mid-block. Usually from a 3-1-3-1-2 structure, they combine through the centre. What is particularly interesting is that Mjällby increasingly use diagonal overloads from the wide zone into the inside, diagonally toward the penalty area, or combine diagonally into the box from a side overload.

Sources indicate that in this case, the overload no longer runs along the touchline but instead follows an imaginary diagonal axis from outside to inside toward the penalty area. The same relational principles are applied as in side overloads, though with a stronger emphasis on diagonal escadinhas and corta luz. One key advantage is that the target zone into which Mjällby combine can be used immediately for a shot. When Mjällby combine from a side overload toward the byline, a cross into the box is usually still required.

Sources indicate that even from side overloads, Mjällby increasingly look for diagonal routes from the touchline into the penalty area through so-called inside diagonals. These create diagonal staggerings of three or more players, which can most easily be played through diagonally using letting the ball run and lay-off combinations. The fact that Mjällby also produce such diagonal breakouts from side overloads naturally makes them less predictable for the opponent. Three example videos of diagonal play within overloads are linked here.

In a recent development, (1) M.H. auf X: „(6/8) Diagonal play against a low-block: Mjällby first create a diagonal overload. Then, from a wide overload, the inside diagonal is played via an escadinha:“ / X.

(1) M.H. auf X: „(7/8) Mjällby create a diagonal overload and combine diagonally toward the center:“ / X.

Recent findings suggest that (1) M.H. auf X: „(8/8) Mjällby consistently create and look for diagonal options.“ / X.

In a recent development, diagonal play is not only a key tool against low blocks. Attentive readers may already have noticed that Mjällby also rely heavily on diagonality against high pressing and deeper pressing, either from wide areas into the centre or from in front of the block through the centre and on to the ball-far side. Why is that? Why does diagonality repeatedly appear as a stylistic element in Mjällby’s play?

Here, only the core ideas behind diagonality in possession play should be outlined. Diagonality combines the progression of verticality with the security of horizontality. This allows progression with greater ball security. In addition, it poses greater challenges for defenders in terms of visual perception. A staggered defence must orient itself while shifting both horizontally and vertically.

Defending teams typically perceive the pitch vertically. Classic formations are structured along an imaginary vertical axis, since play is logically thought of from goal to goal. The attacking team usually also looks to combine vertically toward the opponent’s goal. If, however, the diagonal is used as the imaginary axis in possession play, new passing angles, lanes and dribbling paths open up, because the opponent primarily closes direct vertical passing lanes toward their own goal. This also implies that if an opponent defends primarily along diagonal lines, a vertical or horizontal possession approach can exploit new passing lanes and gaps.

In a recent development, for the attacking team, diagonality means that multiple vertical layers can be bypassed at once, while the body orientation of the receiving player is optimal for the next action, as the ball can be taken forward immediately with the open foot. Visually, the attacker can simultaneously see the ball, a large proportion of teammates and the opponent’s goal. This, in turn, allows for more effective combination play even in tight spaces.

For those interested in the topic, which I was only able to touch on briefly here, I have linked a selection of articles on diagonality below.

https://spielverlagerung.com/2025/06/12/tactical-theory-diagonality/.

https://spielverlagerung.com/2025/06/12/chat-gpt-diagonality-footballs-hidden-dimension-of-play/.

https://medium.com/@stirlingj1982/the-diagonalist-manifesto-610bf3fbca15.

https://jogofuncional1.blogspot.com/2025/12/the-art-of-diagonals.html?m=1.

Mjällby AIF show several distinctive characteristics in possession. In build-up play against high pressing, it is rare to observe exactly the same strategy. Not only can the spacing vary significantly, but the opponent’s pressing is analysed in advance to identify specific weaknesses and define targeted zones to be exploited. The centre is the heart of Mjällby’s build-up, enabling them to play through the opponent’s press with great effectiveness.

Industry observers note that against a mid-block, the central players take on a key role. Mjällby aim to combine through the centre whenever possible. In doing so, the central players constantly attack latest passing lanes, open spaces and then reoccupy them. This makes them difficult for the opponent to pin down and allows them to evade defensive access. With four flexible central players who can be arranged in a wide variety of structures, along with striker Bergström and, situationally, a fullback, Mjällby possess a unique possession-based approach simply through the number of players they deploy in central areas.

It has been revealed that their approach against a low block is particularly striking. Here, Mjällby rely on combinations within pressure-based overloads. The tight spacing has the advantage of placing a large number of players close to the ball immediately after turnovers, making counterpressing far more effective and allowing the opponent to be suffocated near their own penalty area. A more recent development is Mjällby’s increasing tendency to combine diagonally from wide areas into the penalty area. These diagonal combinations are significantly harder to defend and add a greater level of unpredictability to Mjällby’s play in the final third.

  • Sources indicate that nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders.
  • Nacua was also suspended earlier this week for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, a suspension he will serve while on IR.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Los Angeles Rams knew they would be without star wide receiver Puka Nacua for at least four games after he was placed on injured reserve, but now it appears that his absence will extend even longer than that. Head coach Sean McVay noted Friday that Nacua had surgery on his MCL and will miss "a couple of months.".

Sources indicate that nacua suffered MCL and PCL sprains on the final offensive snap of the team's Week 9 win over the Washington Commanders. He took a handoff on third-and-11 and ran it for a 5-yard gain but was injured on the play. He was placed on injured reserve after the injury, which is apparently more serious than initially appeared, given that it required surgery.

Nacua was also suspended earlier this week for three games for violating the league's personal conduct policy, a suspension he will serve while on IR. The NFL did not disclose the nature of his violation, but it's believed that the suspension is related to his ongoing civil suit, which stems from allegations that he bit a woman and made an antisemitic remark.

The NFL did not know that Nacua had potentially season-ending surgery when it suspended him for three games, according to The Athletic.

Industry observers note that now, the Rams will likely be without Nacua for at least the remainder of the regular season. They're on their bye in Week 11 but return in Week 12 to take on the Green Bay Packers in a Wednesday game the night before Thanksgiving. They'll close out their season with games against the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Seattle Seahawks, Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Seahawks again.

The Rams are likely to get fellow wide receiver Davante Adams and tight end Terrance Ferguson back from injured reserve when they return from their bye, or shortly after that. Adams has been out since Week 6 with a hamstring injury, while Ferguson has been out since Week 4 with an ankle injury and then a hamstring ailment he suffered during his 21-day practice window.

The Rams will desperately need each of them to play significant pass-catching roles, as last week they were left with only Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, rookie CJ Daniels and practice-squad signee Xavier Smith at wide receiver. That's alongside Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Davis Allen and Max Klare at tight end for their victory over the division rival Arizona Cardinals.

LA has been beset by injury issues this season, with not only Adams, Ferguson and Nacua missing time on offense but also Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford and Kamren Kinchens sitting out on defense. The Rams were expected to be arguably the best team in the NFL this season after trading for Garrett and bringing Donald out of retirement, but they will instead have to fight for their playoff lives down the stretch of the regular season — and do so without the services of their top pass-catcher.

In a recent development, it has been a surprisingly productive week for the Minnesota Twins. First, catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted the $23.15 million qualifying offer on Tuesday. Jeffers turned down a multi-year offer from the Twins, according to The Athletic, so he's betting on himself. Betting that he'll at least maintain his free agent stock and get paid next offseason.

Then, on Wednesday, the Twins brought back veteran righty Sonny Gray with a two-year contract worth $55 million. There's an opt-out after the first year. Gray, 37, finished fifth in the AL Cy Young voting this season and pitched wonderfully for the Twins in 2022 and 2023. He joins a rotation that, on paper, looks like one of the better starting units in the American League.

Here is Minnesota's rotation depth chart:.

In a recent development, "I really don't take it lightly that he chose us," GM Jeremy Zoll told the Associated Press about Gray's return. "He had an abundance of options, and given where he's at in his career, I know how notable it is to him. He expressed it quite directly how important it is to win, and this isn't just about having a good season or a winning season. It's about winning and going deep in the playoffs and making a real playoff run.".

It has been revealed that matthews could land in the bullpen next season and that might be his long-term home. His stuff should be well suited to a relief role. Gray makes the rotation better and potentially the bullpen better as well by bumping Matthews to relief. Jeffers accepting the qualifying offer keeps a key middle-of-the-order bat in place. A good week for the Twins, this has been.

In a recent development, after a disappointing 77-85 finish this year, Minnesota has already improved significantly in the early days of the offseason. They play in the AL Central. With all due respect, it is not the most imposing division. There's no reason the Twins can't be in the division and wild card races next season. Here now is what's left on Minnesota's offseason to-do list.

Teams had until 5 p.m. ET Friday to offer their pre-arbitration and arbitration-eligible players contracts for 2027. They didn't have to sign them Friday, but they had to tender an offer; otherwise, the player immediately became a free agent. Dozens of players were cut loose at the non-tender deadline, as usual, and two players stood out as non-tender candidates for the Twins: Trevor Larnach and Royce Lewis. Larnach was indeed non-tendered, while Lewis was dealt to the Dodgers.

It's not often a player gets non-tendered after posting a .352 on-base percentage and 120 OPS+, but the writing was on the wall. The Twins had an agreement in place to trade Larnach at the deadline (Astros owner Jim Crane nixed the deal) and they have a very crowded outfield. Also, Larnach had wrist surgery earlier this month. That created some questions going into next season, and the Twins opted to cut him loose.

Industry observers note that larnach had one more year of control remaining and was expected to make over $6 million through arbitration in 2027. I reckon the Twins tried again to trade him prior to Friday's non-tender deadline. In the end, he was non-tendered rather than risk tying $6 million or so up in yet another outfielder, particularly one who is coming off wrist surgery.

Sources indicate that things got so bad this summer that Lewis, who has a .288 on-base percentage in over 1,200 plate appearances the last three years, was sent to Triple-A for a spell, and also moved across the diamond from third base to first base. The Twins could not count on him to provide offense and now he's playing a position with a high offensive bar. That made him expendable.

Lewis, 27, was under team control through 2028 and that extra year was an important consideration for the club. His salary would have been in the $5 million range next season through arbitration, which is pricey but not exorbitant. Now, Lewis will receive a fresh start with the Dodgers, where he can be one of the guys, not the former No. 1 overall pick and expected face of the franchise.

The Twins presumably did not want to give up on a player with as much talent as Lewis. At the same time, they kept trying, and it never worked.

Industry observers note that the Twins got a head start on their offseason bullpen shopping when they acquired Jeff Hoffman at the trade deadline. He has one more year remaining on the contract and will be in the team's late-inning mix in 2027.

Here is manager Derek Shelton's bullpen unit at the moment:.

Morris is not yet a household name, but he has a great arm and was dominant at times in 2026. The Twins have themselves a nice little late-inning trio in Gómez, Hoffman, and Morris. A spare starter like Matthews or Prielipp could wind up in the bullpen as well. Given the quality of their stuff, they have a chance to make a real impact as relievers.

It has been revealed that clearly though, the middle relief could use some help, and the Twins wouldn't need to spend big dollars to improve it. A second-tier free agent like, say, Andrew Kittredge would be a solid pickup. It's worth giving the Miami Marlins a call to see what it would take to get Anthony Bender and/or Michael Petersen. Point is, the bullpen can be improved, for sure.

According to recent reports, the Twins have way more outfielders than outfield spots and that is in no way a bad thing. First and foremost, it allows them to use Byron Buxton as the full-time DH, which could help keep him on the field. Secondly, there's no such thing as too many good players. Depth is important and the Twins certainly have plenty of it in the outfield.

In a recent development, more outfielders than outfield spots is not a problem. It's just something the Twins have to figure out. Even if we assume Buxton will DH and is not part of the outfield mix, here are the outfielders Minnesota must sort through:.

Rodriguez is one of the game's 50 or so best prospects and he is out of minor league options, meaning he must go through waivers to go to Triple-A. Obviously, the Twins won't waive him. Non-tendering Larnach allows the Twins to play Rodriguez alongside Jenkins and Keaschall in the outfield, keep Kreidler and Martin on the bench, and keep the others in Triple-A.

Timberwolves, Grizzlies reportedly hope to move to Eastern Conference after expansion; who makes more sense?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1465 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two fresh teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30.
  • According to recent reports, several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic.
  • In a recent development, getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the NBA is barreling toward expansion, and the addition of two fresh teams would have enormous basketball implications for the remaining 30. Perhaps the biggest is geographic. Both Seattle and Las Vegas are located firmly in the western half of the United States. Should those cities eventually be granted teams, they would play in the Western Conference, leaving the league with unbalanced conferences. Therefore, someone in the West would have to move to the East in order to balance the conferences at 16 teams apiece.

According to recent reports, several teams are eager to do so, according to The Athletic. While the New Orleans Pelicans are not out of the running, the likeliest teams to move in realignment, for now, are reportedly the Minnesota Timberwolves and Memphis Grizzlies.

In a recent development, getting out of the West would be appealing on several levels. Of course, there are obvious basketball reasons for preferring the East. Putting aside the decades of Western Conference superiority that hold little weight in the long run, the two teams best positioned to succeed over the next decade or so are the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder. As the Latest York Knicks learned last June, the easiest path to a championship is avoiding Victor Wembanyama and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander until they've already spent seven games battling each other.

Industry observers note that but this isn't just a basketball conversation. The NBA, like most major American professional sports leagues, tilts east. There are simply more major cities in the Eastern half of the country than the Western half. Of the league's 30 existing teams, 17 play east of the Mississippi River: the 15 already in the Eastern Conference, along with the Timberwolves and Grizzlies.

Sources indicate that travel is simply easier playing in the East. One projection of how many total miles each NBA team will travel this season has only the Miami Heat in the top half of the league, with the other 14 slots belonging to Western Conference teams. That projection has the Heat crossing 24 time zones, while every Western Conference team crosses at least 36.

So Minnesota, Memphis and Fresh Orleans are all incentivized to move, and with the Grizzlies and Timberwolves seemingly favored, let's evaluate the cases for each.

It has been revealed that the fundamental case for the Grizzlies is geographic. Memphis is further East than Minneapolis. As The Athletic points out, it is closer to more Eastern Conference teams as well, as it is within 600 miles of five East teams (Charlotte Hornets, Atlanta Hawks, Indiana Pacers, Chicago Bulls and Milwaukee Bucks). This not only makes travel easier for the Grizzlies, but for those teams as well.

According to recent reports, while the Timberwolves are considered the better team right now, Memphis is probably the team better positioned to be competitive in the long run. Minnesota's best players -- Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Ayo Dosunmu -- are all in their mid-20s earning market-rate salaries, and Rudy Gobert is much older at 34. Plus, the Timberwolves are essentially devoid of first-round draft capital.

The Grizzlies have a significant draft surplus, and their best players -- Cameron Boozer, Cedric Coward and Zach Edey -- are still on their rookie deals. If the idea is balancing the two conferences competitively, even if the Timberwolves have a higher immediate upside, the Grizzlies are probably the team we should expect to contend longer.

According to recent reports, and then there's the matter of maintaining established rivalries. While neither the Grizzlies nor the Timberwolves are franchises steeped in historical success, Minnesota's last few years have established the Timberwolves as genuine postseason rivals to several key Western Conference teams. They've faced Nikola Jokiċ and the Denver Nuggets in multiple recent playoff series. They've faced Luka Dončić in multiple recent playoff series, even if they've come against different teams. Their series against the Spurs last spring included a Wembanyama ejection.

According to recent reports, the NBA may prefer to maximize the number of games Edwards plays against these high-profile opponents because there are existing narratives surrounding those matchups. In that case, keeping the Timberwolves in the West makes sense while allowing the Grizzlies to shift to the East.

Industry observers note that minnesota's geographic case is a bit more nuanced. While Memphis is closer to more teams, Minnesota is closer to a few geographically convenient ones. If we assume for the moment that the new, 16-team conferences are going to come with four divisions featuring four teams each, Minnesota's proximity to Milwaukee, Chicago and Indiana makes for an easy four-team pod.

It has been revealed that the rest of the conference becomes remarkably easy to group from there. We have three more roughly Midwestern teams (Cleveland, Toronto and Detroit), five in the Northeast (Upcoming York, Brooklyn, Boston, Philadelphia and Washington) and four in the Southeast (Charlotte, Miami, Orlando and Atlanta). Just move one of those Northeastern teams to the Midwestern group -- presumably Washington, as it doesn't play in the existing Atlantic Division -- and you're set. If the NBA wants to make divisions a more prominent part of scheduling moving forward, Minnesota makes doing so much easier.

It has been revealed that there's also the idea of giving Edwards, one of the league's more personable stars, an easier path to the NBA Finals by getting him away from Wembanyama and Gilgeous-Alexander. The NBA is, ultimately, a star business, and if stacking the deck in Edwards' favor helps build him up as one of the faces of the league, there is obvious appeal in doing so.

In a recent development, by all accounts, we are far closer to resolution on a Las Vegas team than to the return of the Sonics in Seattle. Bidding has seemingly been more robust in Las Vegas, and an announcement is expected in the near future. If an announcement on Vegas comes before one in Seattle, there will be a brief period in which the NBA has an odd number of planned franchises.

Recent findings suggest that that does not mean that it will ever actually play a season with only 31 teams. Seattle, as commissioner Adam Silver has described, is much more of a turnkey operation than Las Vegas because of its arena situation and preexisting basketball history. In theory, a Seattle team could be announced much later than a Las Vegas team and still begin play in the same season. For now, the reported target for expansion teams to tip off is the 2028-29 season. However, if Seattle's bidding process takes too long for the two to begin play at the same time, or worse, if no Seattle group manages to put forth an acceptable bid in the near future, the possibility of one or even multiple seasons with 31 teams rather than the expected 32 probably does exist.

The NBA -- and every other major American professional sports league -- has had unbalanced conferences in the past. None do now. It creates scheduling headaches, and it's just blatantly unfair. Forcing some teams to overcome 15 opponents to reach the Finals while others only have to top 14 makes playing in the smaller conference too much of an advantage, and since the conference presently believed to be the superior one (the West) would be getting the Las Vegas team, competitive balance would go from a problem to an outright crisis.

Industry observers note that fans have been calling for the abolition of conferences for decades now. Getting it to actually pass a vote would be harder. Realignment is voted on by the board of governors, so abolishing the conferences theoretically would be as well. Eastern Conference owners love having an easier path to the playoffs and the gate revenue those postseason games generate. This is where the idea of a season or two with just 31 teams in the league carries some appeal. It could give the NBA an opportunity to test the abolition of conferences provisionally with the idea that conferences would return when the league reaches 32 unless a new vote determines otherwise.

The appeal of removing conferences altogether stems from the inherent fairness of a playoff system determined solely by record. There have been concerns about how removing the geographic component of playoff scheduling would affect travel, but there are potential solutions there. Returning to the "2-3-2" home-court format would minimize travel, or higher seeds could be allowed to select opponents in the early rounds to decide for themselves how they'd like to prioritize travel. The odds are obviously against the removal of conferences altogether, but expansion offers a potential opportunity to test it without committing to it long-term, and that's an opportunity the NBA would be foolish not to at least explore.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • After winning just one of its first nine games during the 2025 season, the New Orleans Saints were able to gain momentum during the second half by winning five of their last eight with newly installed rookie quarterback Tyler Shough.
  • One of those decisions was selecting Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson at No.
  • Tyson emerged from the pre-draft process as WR1 on my personal board, but his unavailability impacted his stock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After winning just one of its first nine games during the 2025 season, the New Orleans Saints were able to gain momentum during the second half by winning five of their last eight with newly installed rookie quarterback Tyler Shough. New Orleans carried that positive spirit into the offseason and made personnel moves in support of the young quarterback.

One of those decisions was selecting Arizona State wide receiver Jordyn Tyson at No. 8 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft.

Tyson emerged from the pre-draft process as WR1 on my personal board, but his unavailability impacted his stock. He missed 20 games, including the entire 2023 season, over four seasons in college. When available, Tyson, who began his collegiate career at Colorado, was one of the most productive receivers in college football. He amassed 158 receptions for 2,282 yards and 22 touchdowns in just three seasons.

Sources indicate that discussions involving Tyson and Ohio State's Carnell Tate, who was taken No. 4 overall, often referred to Tate as the bigger receiver and Tyson as the more explosive option. But this failed to acknowledge that Tyson was similar in size to Tate.

The sample size is small, but Tyson has been impactful in two games played. He has been targeted on 38.3% of routes run for 120 yards. His usage has been a near-even split between the slot and the boundary.

Sources indicate that tyson comes from an athletic family — he's the brother of Cleveland Cavaliers guard Jaylon Tyson — and it's noticeable. Jordyn is explosive in and out of his breaks. He will run through arm tackles after the catch and has the range to go high or low. His route-running has been inconsistent, but he does not tip his breaks. Tyson will attack the ball in the air, but he did have a fumble in the Browns game.

Jordyn Tyson first down ➡️📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/8PnWK6dh4K.

Newly introduced Orleans was reportedly interested in LSU cornerback Mansoor Delane before Kansas City traded up. Miami edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. was another player commonly linked to the NFC franchise. Bain has been underwhelming thus far.

Tyson's production will not compare to the Browns' Denzel Boston or K.C. Concepcion, or even Tate. He missed too many games so far this season, but Tyson belongs in the conversation from a sheer talent perspective. He is a fluid athlete with a legitimate ability to evade would-be tacklers.

Injuries are difficult, if not impossible, to predict, so projecting Tyson's career would be reckless. Availability will always be the hot topic regarding Tyson, but on-field performance has justified the Saints' belief in him as a top-10 overall talent.

Royce Lewis trade grades: Dodgers land former No. 1 pick; Twins get another arm, arrow-up prospect

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No.
  • Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline.
  • Industry observers note that the Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the Los Angeles Dodgers have added a former No. 1 overall pick. The Dodgers are set to acquire infielder Royce Lewis from the Minnesota Twins for right-hander Bobby Miller and minor-league catcher Francisco Espinoza, reports the Newly introduced York Post. Neither team has revealed the trade.

Lewis, 27, was a candidate to be non-tendered prior to Friday's deadline. Rather than cut him loose, the Twins were able to find a trade partner and receive something in return. The No. 1 pick in the 2017 draft has battled injuries throughout his career and posted a .288 on-base percentage the last three years. Lewis simply failed to launch with Minnesota.

Industry observers note that the Dodgers figure to use Lewis as a platoon partner for Max Muncy at third base and could also move him around the infield as a utility guy. The Twins moved him from third base to first base this past season. Lewis has played every infield position in the substantial leagues, though he's had only one inning at shortstop since 2022.

Miller, 27, has been unable to build on his dynamic 2022 rookie season, when he threw 124 ⅓ innings with a 3.76 ERA. He has battled injuries and control complications since then, and the Dodgers moved him into the bullpen this past season. Miller has a 7.75 ERA in 134 ⅔ Triple-A innings the last three years and can be optioned down in 2027.

Espinoza, 19, reached Low Class-A in 2026 and hit .317/.411/.422 with three home runs and strong contact rates in 46 games. He does not rank among the top 30 Dodgers prospects at Baseball America or MLB Pipeline, but Espinoza is an arrow-up prospect and a solid return for a non-tender candidate.

Here now are our grades for the two-for-one trade.

At worst, Lewis will be a high-priced utility guy next season. He's projected to make $5 million or so through arbitration and that simply is not much for the Dodgers, who have a history of getting underperforming hitters to the next level (like Muncy). At best, Lewis could be the newly introduced Chris Taylor and reach his offensive ceiling while bouncing between positions.

It has been revealed that espinoza is a good prospect, not a great prospect, and Miller is a reclamation project. Those are easy players for the Dodgers to surrender to take a chance on Lewis and his upside. It may not work. Lewis could continue to get hurt and not hit, but it was a low-cost move and the chance of a reward is significant.

It's a very nice upside play for a team that has hit on a lot of upside plays over the year.

It's a bummer things didn't work out for Lewis and the Twins, but the reality is he was a non-tender candidate, and it wasn't a secret. Minnesota was able to get back a solid prospect in Espinoza and a lottery ticket arm in Miller despite having little leverage. Getting two players for Lewis is a very good outcome under the circumstances.

Giving each team an "A" suggests a win-win, and maybe it will be. There's a chance it's a lose-lose, though. Lewis may not hit, Miller may never rediscover his 2022 form, and Espinoza may not pan out. I see the vision for both teams, though and like it.

The Dodgers rolled the dice on a talented player and the Twins were able to fetch two players for someone they might have otherwise cut loose and sent into free agency.

Newcastle kit fiasco sums up haphazard pre-season

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.
  • The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.
  • During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Newcastle’s pre-season friendly against Bayer Leverkusen at St James’ Park took a bizarre turn when a kit clash prompted the hosts to change shirts midway through the first half.

The German team’s white away kit with blue trim proved hard to distinguish from Newcastle’s home strip, which has a white back and blue stripes across the shoulders.

During the first-half hydration break, Newcastle decided to change into their lilac third kit, which improved the viewing experience for fans who took to social media to question the original choice of kits.

Newcastle would go on to lose the game 2-1 in fresh manager Matthias Jaissle’s first game at St James’, a result which followed a 3-1 reverse against Everton on Wednesday evening.

Leverkusen, the 2023-24 Bundesliga champions now managed by Spaniard Carles Martínez Novell, scored after just 44 seconds through a powerful Ibrahim Maza strike.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle’s team found their feet as the first 45 minutes progressed, with Yoane Wissa their biggest attacking threat. The striker endured a difficult first season at the club, but his performances at the World Cup with DR Congo appear to have restored confidence.

It has been revealed that newcastle were level just before half-time, when Malick Thiaw rose highest to plant home a back-post header from a corner. Former Brentford goalkeeper Mark Flekken appealed in vain for a foul, but there was no infringement.

After changing all 10 outfield players at half-time against Everton, Jaissle was more circumspect with second-half substitutes; Rory Finneran for Lewis Miley was the only change before the 80th minute.

Newcastle faded though, and the game was won by Victor Boniface scoring just a few minutes after coming on as a substitute. The Nigeria striker wrong-footed Sean Steur with an impudent piece of skill before rolling the ball into the bottom corner.

Recent findings suggest that the North-East club are coming to terms with the departures of Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães this summer, as well as manager Eddie Howe. They have one more pre-season friendly to play, against Strasbourg on Sunday, before they begin their Premier League campaign at home to Liverpool.

Sources indicate that newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; M Miley (Pivas 81), Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley (Finneran h-t); Elanga, Woltemade (Neave 86), Barnes; Wissa. Subs Charlton, Harris (g), Sanusi, Johnson.

Bayer Leverkusen (4-2-3-1) Flekken; Vazquez (Tape h-t), Bade, Tapsoba, Gutierrez (Belocian 70); Garcia, Fernandez (Terrier 70); Maza (Boniface 80), Tillman (Doganay 70), Moreira (Tella 80); Kofane (Schick h-t). Subs Hofmann, Arthur, Oermann, Poku, Blaswich (g), Alfa-Ruprecht, Hawighorst, Lomb (g).

Referee Michael Oliver (Durham). Attendance 39,059.

A second pre-season defeat in a week for Newcastle. Just like against Everton, they faded in the second 45 minutes but Jaissle decided to leave some tired legs out there for fitness purposes. The performances of Barnes and Wissa were promising, but Newcaslte are giving up chances.

Newcastle had a free-kick with the last kick of the game, but Harvey Barnes loops the delivery straight into Flekken’s gloves.

Schik with a chance to wrap up the victory, but Hornicek saves before Thiaw clears to deny Terrier a tap in on the rebounds.

There will be just three minutes of added time to play.

In a recent development, elanga fouled near the touchline, but time is running out. The free-kick won by Neave came to nothing.

Sources indicate that chance for Barnes! Good combination play involving Elanga and Wissa down the right, and the ball flashed across the six-yard box. Barnes almost steered it in, but did not make firm enough contact.

According to recent reports, newcastle attacking with more urgency since conceding, but there are moans and groans in the ground at a misplaced Elanga pass. Sean Neave has just replaced Woltemade, and the 19-year-old wins a free-kick in a crossing position with his first action of the game.

Industry observers note that the striker has only been on the pitch a few minutes, but Boniface has restored Leverkusen’s lead. Lovely chop inside the box, which sent Steur for a hot dog, before passing the ball into the far corner. No celebration of note from a player who could be on the move this summer.

Newcastle making just their second change of the game: Pivas replaces Mason Miley at right-back.

Leverkusen have made two more changes: Moreira and Maza off, Tella and Boniface on.

The corner is straight down the throat of Flekken, and that prompsts some groans from the home fans.

In a recent development, newcastle having to defend deep for long periods, but Elanga did well to win a free-kick with little support. Moreira dragged the winger down. Then Wissa’s cross is turned behind for a corner.

Recent findings suggest that woltemade’s control lets him down as he tries to bring the ball down on halfway. The game is being played at a snail’s pace at the moment, but Leverkusen are dominating the ball.

Sources indicate that play has now resumed. Garcia does well to defend after Lewis Hall won the ball back in a dangerous position.

Time for another hydration break and Leverkusen are making three more substitutions. We await further changes from Jaissle. Should the game finish level, there will be a penalty shoot-out to decide the winner of the Visit Malta Cup.

In a recent development, rather like the mid-week friendly against Everton, Newcastle have faded after half-time. Struggling to get into the game in any meaningful way. Slick football from Leverkusen but Fernandez fails to bring the ball under his spell in the box when there was time and space to shoot.

Leverkusen just inches away from regaining the lead. It was an incisive run off the left from Afonso Moreira, who tried to place the ball into the far corner but his attempt rolled just wide of the post.

Good defensive header by Lewis Hall before Wissa wins a foul on halfway. Newcastle feeding off scraps at the moment. Elanga goes too early and is flagged offside.

It has been revealed that bayer Leverkusen have had the better of it in this half, but some of the shooting has been wayward. This time is it Schik’s turn to slash a shot over the bar. Fouls committed by Finneran and Botman.

Newcastle with a three-on-three on the break after Wissa does well to win the ball back on halfway, but Woltemade was too slow to get his shot away at the end of the move. More good play from Wissa.

Half a chance for Fernandez to shoot from the edge of the D, but he was leaning back and ballooned the shot miles over the bar.

It has been revealed that finneran, the youngster in Newcastle’s midfield, is caught on the ball but then does well to recover it. I reckon there will be a raft of changes on the hour mark.

In a recent development, corner for Leverkusen after Moreira gets forward and attacks Mason Miley. The German side have additional aerial threat with Schik on the pitch. Woltemade does well to head clear.

Bayer Leverkuen kick off in the second half.

Jaissle made 10 against Everton, so wants his starters to build minutes today. Rory Finneran is coming on for Newcastle, an 18-year-old academy player. He replaces Lewis Miley in midfield. Czech striker Patrik Schik is on for Bayer Leverkusen.

Recent findings suggest that the scoreline is a fair reflection of an even first half, with Wissa Newcastle’s best player. The story though, is that kit clash that prompted Newcastle to change into their lilac third kit halfway through the half.

Just the two minutes of stoppage time to play.

Sources indicate that newcastle equalise from a set-piece. Flekken is claiming a foul, but it is a legitimate goal. The goalkeeper was nowhere to be seen on a corner that looped all the way to be back post, and he seemed to lose his bearings allowing Thiaw to find the far corner.

Industry observers note that newcastle have a corner after another move in which Wissa was lively. His performances have been a ray of light in pre-season, he really struggled in his first season at the club.

Lewis Hall takes the free-kick, but he scoops it well over the bar. Elanga delivers a low cross from the right, but Garcia is well positioned to clear.

Newcastle enjoying a lot more possession now, but you cannot say they look like equalising.

That was better though, more zip in the attack with Elanga laying the ball off for Wissa and Fernandez is booked from dragging the Newcastle forward to the ground. Free-kick in a shooting position.

In a recent development, good play from Lewis Hall, skipping beyond two challenges to escape from a tight spot but then his crossfield pass is intercepted. Moreira passes the ball straight out of play for a Newcastle goal kick, when there was a chance for Leverkusen to punish the hosts on the break.

It has been revealed that elanga tries to take on Gutierrez but his low cross is too close to Flekken. Gutierrez then buys a foul when under pressure from Lewis Miley. Game has become quite bitty following those stoppages. Maza then chops down Harvery Barnes.

According to recent reports, the game is back under way. Changing kits has improved things visually but it is still not ideal. You wonder how on earth two clubs of this stature failed to liaise on this before the game.

Bayer Leverkusen are still on top, but play has been stopped for a hydration break. Some boos from the stands, it is not an especially hot day.

It has been revealed that on the subject of the kit clash, Newcastle are now changing into their lilac away kit. Shades of Manchester United at the Dell all those years ago.

In a recent development, A short stoppage in play after Tapsoba receives a knock in the small of the back from Newcastle’s goalkeeper Hornicek. Both managers get their players over for a tactical conflab.

Industry observers note that leverkusen look very accomplished in possession, they are moving the ball well through the lines. Kofane was a major threat when they played Arsenal in last season’s Champions League and they are looking to find him with crosses. Mason Miley defends well at right-back, but at the expense of a corner.

Flekken called into action again, Newcastle starting to warm to their task. It was direct play from first Elanga and then Barnes, but his cross deflects towards the goalkeeper and he parries away. Then Barnes is fouled, and Newcastle have a free-kick in a crossing position near the left corner of the penalty area. Poor delivery from Barnes, Flekken claims.

Newcastle fans sing “walking in a Keegan wonderland” in unison. Bade is then penalised for catching Woltemade late as they contested an aerial challenge.

Newcastle’s best moment so far: Wissa peels off the shoulder of Bade and tested Flekken with a volley from a tight angle. The goalkeeper saved and Leverkusen scramble clear, but it was good movement from the Newcastle striker.

Leverkusen continue to make the running, enjoying more possession and most of it is coming inside Newcastle’s half. Goalkeeper Flekken takes a beat inside his own six-yard box, and his pass out is almost cut out by Woltemade.

Newcastle’s players are wearing black armbands in memory of Kevin Keegan.

There is a slightly awkward clash of kits on display: both shirts feature a lot of white, and the blue trim around the shoulders of Newcastle’s home kit is quite similar to Leverkusen’s away strip.

Kofane, who impressed up front last season in Germany, throws himself at a cross.

Industry observers note that fans were barely settled in their seats when Maza’s vicious left-footed strike from outside of the area flew past Hornicek. Cracking goal, not much the goalkeeper could do about it.

Newcastle get the game under way.

Matthias Jaissle walks to the home dugout for the first time as manager. Just eight days until the proper stuff begins against Liverpool, a fixture which tends to throw up entertaining games. Bayer Leverkusen keep the home players waiting in the tunnel.

The former Liverpool defender has been linked with a move to Arsenal this week. Quansah is with his team-mates but not part of the matchday squad.

Bayer Leverkusen XI: Flekken; Gutierrez, Bade, Fernandez, Moreira, Tillman, Tapsoba, Arthur, Garcia, Maza, Kofane.

Subs: Blaswich, Lomb, Hofmann, Terrier, Schick, Oermann, Tape, Poku, Vazquez, Boniface, Tella, Alfa-Ruprecht, Doganay, Hawighorst.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; M Miley, Thiaw (c), Botman, Hall; Steur, L Miley; Elanga, Woltemade, Barnes; Wissa.

Subs: Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Sanusi, Johnson, Finneran, Neave.

Today's team to take on Bayer Leverkusen in the @VisitMalta Weekender 👊 pic.twitter.com/ZfRvucBXSq.

Newcastle United continue their preparations for the upcoming season with a home friendly against Bayer Leverkusen, hoping to improve on their pretty limp showing against Everton at Murrayfield.

Recent findings suggest that new manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the Premier League season, insisting that he sees opportunity in the situation. Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who had lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a major challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

In a recent development, “We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

Sources indicate that “Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

In a recent development, “Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

Industry observers note that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he noted.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.
